messages:
anya: Heads-up — did some spike analysis this morning. We had two tenants emitting sustained ~3x baseline RPS for 12m, latency stayed ok but queue depth jumped and we saw tail token cost climb.

mike: Link? can you drop the graph?

anya: https://redwood.internal/dash/tenants/compare?span=24h — the two orange lines are tenant-A and tenant-B. Notice the CPU stable but per-tenant wait_time p95 spikes.

sloane: Looks like a classic noisy neighbor. Were these background batch jobs or interactive?

anya: Tenant-A is interactive, high concurrency; Tenant-B is model-rerank batch-ish that started triggering more streaming requests.

samir: We should avoid hard throttles for interactive tenants. Idea: deprioritize burst traffic by inserting a burst-signal tag and letting routing reduce priority rather than dropping tokens. Thoughts?

mike: +1. Deprioritization preserves good UX for low-latency calls. How would that work with current credit allocator?

samir: Proposal sketch: add a short-lived "burst_score" metric per key (exponentially weighted). If score > threshold, route requests to deprioritized queue that has lower concurrency and smaller batch windows. Not a hard deny, but slower and cheaper kernels.

anya: That pairs nicely with per-route QoS. We can mark streaming vs non-streaming and let streaming keep a fast-path unless burst_score high.

infra-bot: deploy/job:quota-checker v2 rolled out to prod-ops at 2026-02-11T09:12Z

eva: What signals feed burst_score? token/sec, inflight, kv-cache-miss-rate? Need to be careful—some models naturally longer tokens.

samir: Agreed. I propose composite: normalized_rps (by tenant baseline), inflight_ratio, latency_p95_surge, and recent_kv_miss_ratio. All EWMA with 30s window and different weights.

mike: Can we avoid per-tenant heavy cardinality in the routing tier? Putting EWMAs in the edge is heavy. Maybe compute burst_score in a lightweight aggregator (ingest sidecar) and push to routing via small header.

anya: We already send cost headers between services. Adding X-Tenant-Burst: <score> should be cheap. Need TTL to avoid stale signals.

sloane: From fairness POV, deprioritization may still let big tenants consume all background capacity if not careful. We need a lower-priority capacity floor per-tenant to avoid starvation.

samir: Good point. Plan: deprioritized queue has two sub-lanes: soft-priority (best-effort) and minimal-guarantee (small guaranteed share). Tunable by tenant class (free/prod/enterprise).

mike: How do we expose this in the console? Ops needs to see current burst_score, assigned lane, and recent demotions. Also a rollout toggle per-cluster.

eva: Dashboard idea: per-tenant timeline with color bands (normal / deprioritized / guaranteed). Alert when deprioritized > 5m for prod tenants.

anya: For rollout: start in read-only routing (observe-only header) for a week, then canary 5% of traffic with deprioritization enabled cluster A. Keep metrics: end-to-end latency p50/p95, successful tokens/second, and errors.

samir: Need a quick playbook: how to revert, and an automated fallback to model-variant with cheaper kernel if deprioritized queue fills. Otherwise heavy tenants could overload cheaper lane too.

mike: Implementation notes: routing change + small sidecar aggregator + console UX. Rough ETA: proto in two sprints. Who owns prototype?

anya: I'll draft the spike for the aggregator and dashboards. Samir can prototype routing header semantics. Mike can do console mockups. Eva will own SLO/alert params.

anya: Action items: 1) Spike aggregator (anya) — 1 sprint. 2) Routing prototype with header handling (samir) — 1 sprint. 3) Dashboard mockups (mike) — 1 sprint. 4) Alert/runbook (eva) — 2 wks.

sloane: Favor experiments with deprioritization over hard quota ejection. Less user-visible pain and better for PLG growth.

infra-bot: incident/notification: auto-alert created for tenant-A sustained deprioritization at 2026-02-11T09:20Z

mike: I'll put a canary flag in the console and add telemetry hooks. We'll also log `burst_score` on traces for correlating trace->score.

anya: Ok let's sync tomorrow 10am to review spike results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
